sentences.en: Zero.

sentences.en: That was probably my strongest performance.

sentences.zh: 那道题我答得非常好，因为我正好在 LLVM 工作过，所以跟浮点数较量过。

sentences.en: Um, but like, it's a terrible interview question that like, it didn't, it shouldn't have been a significant factor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但它是个糟糕的面试题，它不应该，它本不该成为一个重要的考量因素。

sentences.en: Um, the other interview question that I remember, um, that I've talked about publicly as just like one of my least favorite interview questions was like,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得的另一个面试题，嗯，我曾在公开场合说过它是我最不喜欢的面试题之一，那就是，

sentences.en: it was the last interview of the day at Google.
sentences.zh: 那是谷歌当天的最后一场面试。

sentences.en: Um, and I, you have to understand like this interview process was horrible for me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你得明白，这个面试流程对我来说简直糟透了。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 而且，那套衣服当然不是我在苹果面试时要穿的，因为在苹果，去苹果面试时你的外表很重要。

sentences.en: Um, and so for my Google interview, I showed up in jeans and my thesis hoodie.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以去谷歌面试时，我穿着牛仔裤和我的毕业论文连帽衫就去了。

sentences.en: Isn't, isn't that like what they expect now?
sentences.zh: 难道，难道现在他们不就期待这样吗？

sentences.en: Like what is a thesis hoodie?
sentences.zh: 话说什么是毕业论文连帽衫？

sentences.en: Well, like, like the, the hoodie I'd been wearing and hadn't had a chance to launder.
sentences.zh: 就是，我一直穿着而且一直没机会洗的那件连帽衫。

sentences.en: That's what I thought.
sentences.zh: 我是这么想的。

sentences.en: That's what I thought.
sentences.zh: 我也是这么想的。

sentences.en: By thesis.

sentences.en: I thought you meant you got like a, you know, I offended my thesis.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你是说你获得了那种，你知道的，我通过了论文答辩。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: slept after flying across the country for one night, got up and like arrived at Google's campus at 9 a.m.
sentences.zh: 飞越大半个国家后睡了一晚，起床后在早上 9 点到达谷歌园区，整个人处于一种被打懵了的状态。

sentences.en: And I'm sitting in a lobby surrounded by people in suits with portfolios, like looking sharp, like for an interview in my jeans and my thesis, like, hoodie.
sentences.zh: 然后我坐在大厅里，周围全是穿着西装、拿着公文包、看起来精明强干的人，就像是去面试一样，而我穿着牛仔裤和我的毕业论文连帽衫。

sentences.en: Hmm.

sentences.en: It was, it was something else.

sentences.zh: 所以最后一个面试官出现了，他一出现就说，我希望你实现 WGET。

sentences.zh: 就像 WGET 这个工具，直接在白板上实现它。

sentences.en: Go, go.
sentences.zh: 开始，开始。

sentences.zh: 所以我看着，就好像，我说，我这辈子从来没做过网络，网络编程。

sentences.en: Like, I literally have not written socket open paren once.

sentences.en: I didn't like, just, it just never came up.
sentences.zh: 我没有，只是，从来没遇到过。

sentences.en: It was not a particular focus of mine in school.
sentences.zh: 那不是我在学校里的重点关注方向。

sentences.en: I just like all the code I'd written.
sentences.zh: 我写的所有代码，

sentences.en: It was all around compilers and video game graphics and not around like networking.
sentences.zh: 基本上都围绕着编译器和电子游戏图形学，而不是围绕网络编程。

sentences.en: And he looks at me.
sentences.zh: 然后他看着我。

sentences.en: It's like, I mean, okay, but like, fine, fine.
sentences.zh: 就好像，好吧，但是，行吧，行吧。

sentences.en: Just walk me through how this, like, like, like you can use pseudocon.
sentences.zh: 你就跟我过一遍这个，就像，就像你可以用伪代码。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: I don't care if you know any network, like, but like walk me through, like what you would need to implement WGET.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎你是否懂任何网络，但是，跟我过一遍你需要如何实现 WGET。

sentences.en: Like, you know, send an HTTP request and get a response.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，发送一个 HTTP 请求并得到一个响应。

sentences.en: And I looked at him, like, like, I do not know anything about the, like, HTTP.
sentences.zh: 我看着他，就像，我对 HTTP 一无所知。

sentences.en: I don't know the protocol.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这个协议。

sentences.en: I have no idea what's needed here.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道这里需要什么。

sentences.en: I don't know how, he blanks at me.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么，他呆呆地看着我。

sentences.en: And he's like, you don't know where you're interviewing, right?
sentences.zh: 然后他说，你不知道你是在哪儿面试吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, that was, that was basically what I was thinking.
sentences.zh: 对，我当时心里基本上就是这么想的。

sentences.en: It's like, this is Google.
sentences.zh: 心想，这里可是谷歌。

sentences.en: And I was like, yes, but I've worked on, like, compilers and programming languages.
sentences.zh: 我说，是的，但我一直从事的是编译器和编程语言方面的工作。

sentences.en: It says so on my resume.
sentences.zh: 我的简历上就是这么写的。

sentences.en: Like, you shouldn't be surprised by this.
sentences.zh: 所以你不应该对此感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I didn't actually, like, claim anything else on my resume.
sentences.zh: 我其实并没有在简历上声称自己懂别的什么。

sentences.en: And the server's going to send a response.

sentences.zh: 那是因为我的开源工作。

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 对，

sentences.zh: 如果没有的话，我提前向我即将让她尴尬的团队成员道个歉，我就不点名了。

sentences.en: But I had somebody who approached me at CppCon a few years ago and said, hey, I think I want to come work at your team.
sentences.zh: 但几年前在 CppCon 上有人找到我，说，嘿，我觉得我想来你们团队工作。

sentences.en: And she did.

sentences.en: And, like, this isn't somebody that I'd known previously.

sentences.en: We'd met at the conference that year.
sentences.zh: 我们是那年在会议上认识的。

sentences.en: I talked a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了一会儿。

sentences.en: I thought she was impressive.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她很让人印象深刻。

sentences.en: She sent me her resume.
sentences.zh: 她把简历发给了我。

sentences.en: And I, like, looked at her resume and her GitHub for about five minutes.
sentences.zh: 我大概花五分钟看了看她的简历和 GitHub。

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, like, I have all the information that I need now.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，对，我现在已经有了我需要的所有信息。

sentences.en: Like, and, like, I, like, there will be interviews that will happen.
sentences.zh: 而且，面试肯定还是会有的，

sentences.en: But, like, I am deciding here at this spot five minutes after looking at this person's resume that I am going to hire this person.
sentences.zh: 但是，我在看完这个人简历五分钟后的这个当口就决定了，我要录用这个人。

sentences.en: And we did hire her.
sentences.zh: 我们确实录用了她。

sentences.en: And it worked out wonderfully.
sentences.zh: 结果非常棒。

sentences.en: And, you know, for, sometimes you just know it's somebody that has, you know, a prolific open source background.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有时候你就是知道这个人有着丰富的开源背景。

sentences.en: And it's just, like, you want that person.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会想要这样的人。

sentences.en: And so because this person who got me to send the resume in in the first place knew about my work in LLPN.
sentences.zh: 所以，因为当初促使我把简历提交上去的这个人了解我在 LLVM 上的工作，

sentences.en: And he knew how the hiring process at Google worked.
sentences.zh: 他也了解谷歌的招聘流程是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And so he made sure that, in addition to my interviews, they also were aware of the open source work.
sentences.zh: 所以他确保除了我的面试之外，他们也了解我的开源工作。

sentences.en: And my understanding is that this was still not especially impressive.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，这其实也算不上特别令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: And I've looked at my open source work from then, and it was not especially impressive.
sentences.zh: 我回看了一下我当时的开源工作，确实不是特别令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: And maybe it was impressive for its time.
sentences.zh: 或许在当时那个年代它算令人印象深刻吧。

sentences.en: No, no, it's a lot of, it's about potential, though.
sentences.zh: 不，不，这很大程度上关乎潜力，你知道的。

sentences.en: You know, like, I think this is, like, one of my skill sets is, like, being able to, like, recognize untapped potential or whatnot.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是，这就像是我的技能之一，能够识别出未被发掘的潜力什么的。

sentences.en: Like, sometimes it's not about what the person's done, but it's about what potential you see in what they've done.

sentences.en: Like, maybe somebody hasn't done a lot, but if they're, like, very early stage career, and at this point in Chandler's life, he would have been very early stage.
sentences.zh: 也许某人还没做太多事情，但如果他们的职业生涯还处于非常早期的阶段，而且在钱德勒人生的这个阶段，他当时正处于非常早期的阶段，

sentences.en: And so you, you know, and honestly, my guess is, because this was somebody that you knew, Chandler, from IRC, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，老实说，我猜，因为这是你在 IRC 上认识的人，钱德勒，对吧？

sentences.en: That it was not somebody that was.
sentences.zh: 这不是那种……

sentences.zh: 就像是在 IRC 上认识的。

sentences.en: Is it somebody that you'd interacted with previously?
sentences.zh: 这是你以前有过互动的人吗？

sentences.en: Only on IRC.
sentences.zh: 只在 IRC 上互动过。

sentences.en: I've never met them face to face.
sentences.zh: 我从未和他们面对面见过。

sentences.en: But it was probably less about the open source contributions that you made, and was probably more about how you'd interacted with that person.
sentences.zh: 但这可能与其说取决于你做过的开源贡献，不如说更多地取决于你与那个人的互动方式。

sentences.en: So the sort of questions you'd asked on that IRC channel.
sentences.zh: 也就是你在那个 IRC 频道上问过的问题类型。

sentences.en: Okay, okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: The sort of discussions.
sentences.zh: 讨论的类型。

sentences.en: Then I have a question.
sentences.zh: 那我有问题了。

sentences.en: Because you have, like, Connor, you can bow out on this one.
sentences.zh: 因为你们有，康纳，这个问题你可以不参与。

sentences.en: But both Bryce and Chandler have met me in real life.
sentences.zh: 但布莱斯和钱德勒都在现实生活中见过我。

sentences.en: You've interacted with me on various media.
sentences.zh: 你们在各种媒体上和我互动过。

sentences.en: And, you know, and maybe watched me speak.

sentences.zh: 我是说，对我而言，这、这、这、这主要是关于，你知道的，施加影响，呃，还有设定方向。

sentences.en: And this is, and this is why you can kind of see this, uh, showing up in, in the kind of questions that I was probing here.

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 呃，当然。

sentences.en: So, you know, uh, uh, an example of this would be your, your, I'll take one from, from my own experience here.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Uh, if we're, if we're, if we're at Google and we're, we're actually using, you know, uh, GCC and at the time the, the compiler is not really meeting Google's needs.
sentences.zh: 呃，如果我们在、在、在谷歌，而且我们实际上在用，你知道的，呃，GCC，而当时这个编译器其实并不能满足谷歌的需求。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Um, actually figuring, realizing that the, the, the, the needs that we have are not for just, just a better compiler, but for, for example,
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上弄明白、意识到我们需要的不仅仅是一个更好的编译器，而是，比如说，

sentences.en: for tools built on top of the compiler in order to help our code base scale and our developers kind of deal with, uh, the challenges of C++.
sentences.zh: 为了在编译器之上构建工具，以帮助我们的代码库规模化，并帮助我们的开发者应对C++的挑战。

sentences.en: It became very clear that we needed a different platform.
sentences.zh: 很显然，我们需要一个不同的平台。

sentences.en: And so one of the things I had to do was to go around and convince everyone at the company that like, no, we're going to,
sentences.zh: 所以我要做的事情之一，就是四处奔走，说服公司里的每个人，不，我们要，

sentences.en: we're going to directionally pivot from building on top of GCC to building on top of Clang and LLVM.
sentences.zh: 我们要从在GCC上构建，方向性地转向在Clang和LLVM上构建。

sentences.en: Not because they're better, uh, at the time they weren't even, they weren't better.
sentences.zh: 不是因为它们更好，呃，当时它们甚至都不是，它们并不更好。

sentences.en: They were actually worse as a compiler.
sentences.zh: 作为一个编译器，它们实际上更糟糕。

sentences.en: Uh, but because they're going to give us the leverage we need, we're going to be able to build the tools we need to build on top of them.
sentences.zh: 呃，但因为它们能给我们带来所需的杠杆作用，我们将能够在其之上构建我们需要的工具。

sentences.en: And so as a direction, we have to kind of pivot the entire company's direction, uh, so that we can build those tools.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一种方向，我们必须顺应方向，改变整个公司的方向，呃，这样我们才能构建这些工具。

sentences.en: So how do you do that?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么做到这一点？

sentences.en: Uh, it, largely it's about presenting, uh, a, a good argument with good evidence to support it to the right people at the right time.
sentences.zh: 呃，很大程度上，就是要在正确的时间向正确的人提出，呃，一个有充分证据支持的、好的论点。

sentences.en: And so you, you have to be able to get into that room, I guess, to those people.
sentences.zh: 所以你，我想你必须能够进入那个房间，去接触那些人。

sentences.en: Uh, that is, that is one thing, uh, you do have to have access to the people who are, who, who you need to kind of convince.
sentences.zh: 呃，这是，这是必须的，呃，你确实必须能够接触到那些你、你、你需要说服的人。

sentences.en: However, at least at Google, that part is, is, is actually probably the easiest part.
sentences.zh: 然而，至少在谷歌，这部分实际上可能是最简单的一部分。

sentences.en: Um, if, if, if you, if you put in enough effort, you can almost certainly talk to anyone at Google that you need to in order to try and convince them of something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果，如果你投入了足够的精力，你几乎肯定能跟谷歌里任何你需要谈话的人交流，以便试图说服他们某事。

sentences.en: Um, it, it's very unlikely that you, you can't find a person that you talk to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你、你找不到可以交流的人，这种可能性非常小。

sentences.en: Um, even if they're kind of, you know, some, some layers that you have to work through, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，哪怕他们可能，你知道的，中间隔着一些层级，对吧？

sentences.en: You can at least find the person at the first layer.
sentences.zh: 你至少能找到第一层的人。

sentences.en: And if you can convince them, they're going to make sure you can talk to the person at the next layer of the company.
sentences.zh: 如果你能说服他们，他们就会确保你能和公司下一层级的人对话。

sentences.en: Uh, and it's an incremental process, right?
sentences.zh: 呃，这是一个渐进的过程，对吧？

sentences.en: This took us, uh, uh, this took probably, I would say six to seven years to really establish this, uh, directional shift at Google, um, fully, right?
sentences.zh: 这花了我们，呃，呃，这大概花了，我可以说花了六到七年的时间，才真正在谷歌完全确立了这种，呃，方向上的转变，对吧？

sentences.en: And there were just a lot of milestones along the way.
sentences.zh: 一路上有很多里程碑。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of, you know, kind of pushing this directional strategy further and further and further at each set stage of this.
sentences.zh: 在每一个阶段，都有很多，你知道的，一直在推进这种方向性战略的发展。

sentences.en: And, and the kind of the, the surprising thing is that even this is the thing I've outlined, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，而且有点让人惊讶的是，甚至连我刚才概述的这件事，对吧？

sentences.en: Changing the, the compiler from one, one technology stack to a different technology stack because of a different set of use cases that we have.
sentences.zh: 因为我们有一套不同的用例，所以把编译器从一个技术栈换到另一个技术栈。

sentences.en: Um, that's actually, that's actually itself just an incremental step that, that, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那其实，那其实本身也只是一个渐进的步骤，对吧？

sentences.en: Like everything kind of decomposes into these kinds of incremental components.
sentences.zh: 就像任何事情都可以分解成这些渐进的组成部分一样。

sentences.en: And so that's actually an incremental step of, you know, changing the direction of the strategy for how we write C++ code at Google, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是一个渐进的步骤，你知道的，改变了我们在谷歌编写C++代码的战略方向，对吧？

sentences.en: And, and, and, uh, another component of that was, uh, Google kind of, uh, becoming much more heavily involved in the standardization process.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，呃，其中的另一个组成部分是，谷歌，呃，变得更加深入地参与到标准化过程中。

sentences.en: Um, and right and try and trying to push on the industry and the standardization process in order to shift C++ and kind of bend C++ towards, uh, being a better,
sentences.zh: 嗯，对吧，并试图推动行业和标准化过程，以便让C++发生转变，某种程度上让C++变得更好，

sentences.en: a better tool for our developers.
sentences.zh: 成为对我们的开发者而言更好的工具。

sentences.en: Um, so I, I think for me, um, I, I think a lot of people tend to think of, like, when we talk about the distinction between leadership and management, people think that means that,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我觉得，对我而言，嗯，我觉得很多人倾向于认为，当我们谈论领导力和管理的区别时，人们认为这意味着，

sentences.en: oh, the, the leadership means having the vision and, and like management is dealing with the people.
sentences.zh: 哦，领导力意味着拥有愿景，而管理则是处理人的问题。

sentences.en: And I don't, I don't, I don't think that's actually the case.
sentences.zh: 而我并不、不、不认为实际情况是这样的。

sentences.en: Um, I think leadership is about recognizing sort of where you want, where, where things need to go and then inspiring people to believe in that vision.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为领导力在于认清事情需要朝哪个方向发展，然后激励人们去相信那个愿景。

sentences.en: Um, so I think it's fundamentally about people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我认为它从根本上来说是关于人的。

sentences.en: It's about, there's a big difference between ordering somebody to do something, saying, do this because I told you to, and inspiring them to do it because you've,
sentences.zh: 它是关于，命令某人去做某事——说“照我说的去做”——与激励他们去做之间有着巨大的区别，因为你已经，

sentences.en: you've convinced them that this is an exciting thing or that this is the right direction to go in or that this is something that they should believe in.
sentences.zh: 你已经让他们相信这是一件令人兴奋的事情，或者这是正确的方向，或者这是他们应该相信的事情。

sentences.en: And I think that's really what leadership is about.
sentences.zh: 我想这才是领导力的真谛。

sentences.en: You have to understand, um, the problem that you need to be solving, you know, the, the, um, the, the business that you're in, what your users need,
sentences.zh: 你必须理解，呃，你需要解决的问题，你知道的，呃、呃、呃，你所在的业务，你的用户需要什么，

sentences.en: and then you need to be able to identify what is the, you know, the solution to that problem.
sentences.zh: 然后你需要能够识别出那个问题的解决方案是什么。

sentences.en: Um, and then you need to get your people to believe in the problem, to believe in your users, to believe in the business, and to believe that the solution is the right way forward.

sentences.en: Um, and I think that my experience may be a bit colored by working so much on, um, uh, community driven projects and standards committees and volunteer organizations,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为我的经历可能有点受到大量参与，呃，呃，由社区驱动的项目、标准委员会以及志愿者组织的经历的影响，

sentences.en: And so perhaps my experience is a bit colored by that, um, of, of, you know, of that,
sentences.zh: 所以也许我的经历有点受到那个的影响，嗯，关于那个，

sentences.en: that the only way that I can get people to do things in a lot of contexts is if I can inspire them to do it, because I can't just tell them to do it.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，我能让别人做事的唯一方法就是激发他们去做，因为我不能直接命令他们去做。

sentences.en: I want to, I want to let everyone in on a secret.

sentences.en: Uh, that's always true.

sentences.en: Um, right.

sentences.zh: 所以我，你知道，在谷歌，我们、我们、我们、我们如今是一家大公司，对吧？

sentences.en: We're a big company.
sentences.zh: 我们是一家大公司。

sentences.zh: 所以，我有一个例子，但我这个例子是因为一些非常悲伤的原因。

sentences.zh: 呃，所以，所以，所以，因为当我注意到你在谈论这个时，其中一件事就是你从来没有真正在谈论，呃，让别人听你的话。

sentences.zh: 而且，而且，而且，所以，所以，所以，所以，我，就像我在思科内部设法做出的转变，我们为会议室构建了这些网真系统。

sentences.en: So, so, so the, the lengths that I had to go to just to get people to listen.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，所以，为了让别人听我说，我不得不付出巨大的努力。

sentences.en: And when I went into the room and I said, the way that we're doing things now, it won't work.
sentences.zh: 当我走进房间说“我们现在做事的方式行不通”时，

sentences.zh: 要让别人真正听进去这一点，是如此艰难，因为没有人，而且，而且，最后，当他们买账我的想法时，

sentences.zh: 他们召集了一个由20名男工程师参加的会议，却没有叫我来。

sentences.en: Um, I, I, I think you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我、我、我认为你完全正确。

sentences.en: Um, and I, it's, you know, I think people like Chandler and I, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，你知道的，我觉得像钱德勒和我，嗯，

sentences.en: I think we, we tend to be loud people who, who, um, you know, we have strong opinions and we don't, we're, we're,
sentences.zh: 我想我们，我们往往是那种声音很大的人，我们、嗯，你知道的，我们有强烈的观点，而且我们不，我们、我们，

sentences.zh: 我们分享这些观点没有任何问题。

sentences.en: Um, and I think because we're, you know, white guys in tech, that's very accepted, accepted, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为因为我们是，你知道的，科技界的白人男性，这非常被接受，对吧？

sentences.en: Um, that, you know, like if, if I,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，如果，如果我，

sentences.en: I spend most of my time going into meetings and pitching people on crazy ideas that nobody believes in yet and trying to convince them to believe in that.
sentences.zh: 我大部分时间都花在开会和向人们推销那些还没人相信的疯狂想法上，并试图说服他们去相信。

sentences.en: And it's easier for me to do that because I know that it's acceptable for me to do that and that, like, I feel confident doing that.
sentences.zh: 对我来说这样做更容易，因为我知道这样做是被接受的，而且，比如，我对此感到自信。

sentences.en: But you, Patricia, as a woman in tech, um, one, uh, you're not going to feel as comfortable doing that because you know that, you know, that there's a huge bias against you.
sentences.zh: 但你，帕特里夏，作为科技界的女性，嗯，第一，你不会觉得这样做那么自在，因为你知道，你知道，对你有巨大的偏见。

sentences.en: Um, and two, it's so much harder for people to listen.
sentences.zh: 第二，要让别人听进去要困难得多。

sentences.en: I would be the one presenting and people would shush me in the meeting.
sentences.zh: 我常常是做展示的那个人，而在会议上人们会嘘我。

sentences.zh: 我曾遇到一个像高管一样的家伙在会上说：“你以为你是谁？”

sentences.en: And I was like, uh, I'm, I'm just here answering a question that you asked me.
sentences.zh: 而我说，呃，我、我只是来回答你刚才问我的一个问题。

sentences.en: I think, I think there's also like, it's, it's weird, right?
sentences.zh: 我想，我想还有一种情况，挺诡异的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because, um, well, one of the, I mean, one of the things that's kind of, I've been fairly lucky with is, uh,
sentences.zh: 因为，嗯，好吧，其中一个，我是说，让我感到挺幸运的事情之一就是，呃，

sentences.en: that the, the, you know, certainly I get a, get a foot in the door,
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道的，我当然能获得一个机会，对吧？

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: But being, by looking like everyone's expected image of, of random geek helps.
sentences.zh: 但长得符合所有人对随机极客的预期形象，这会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Um, but I think it's important for people to realize that, um, that, that helps and it makes a big difference.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为让人意识到这一点很重要，嗯，这确实有帮助，而且有很大区别。

sentences.en: But I actually think the goal and like the challenge is, is, it's structurally the same.
sentences.zh: 但我实际上认为目标以及挑战，在结构上是一样的。

sentences.en: It's a difference.
sentences.zh: 有区别。

sentences.en: It's a, it's different than magnitude, a big difference in magnitude, but you still have to convince people to listen to you.
sentences.zh: 这是量级的不同，量级上有很大的不同，但你仍然必须说服别人听你的。

sentences.en: Well, the thing is, the thing is, in the end, the way, the way I won was by proving my point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题是，问题是，到头来，我赢得认同的方式是通过证明我的观点。

sentences.en: I didn't win by convincing anyone.
sentences.zh: 我不是靠说服任何人赢得认同的。

sentences.en: Like I, I, I convinced them by, by proving the math.
sentences.zh: 就像我，我，我通过用数学证明来让他们信服。

sentences.en: I didn't convince them because they believed in me.
sentences.zh: 我不是因为他们相信我而说服了他们。

sentences.en: They didn't believe in me at all.
sentences.zh: 他们一点也不相信我。

sentences.en: What I managed to do was to prove by implementing by it, because what I was saying was not, and no matter how much research and no matter how much I would present,
sentences.zh: 我设法做到的是通过实际实现来证明，因为我所说的话并不是，无论做多少研究，无论我做多少展示，

sentences.en: nobody would believe me.
sentences.zh: 都没有人会相信我。

sentences.en: So the only, and, and this is the reason why I won.
sentences.zh: 所以唯一的，而且，这也是我获胜的原因。

sentences.en: And this is also one of the reasons why I think women have to be engineers, uh, because I won because I could make it.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我认为女性必须成为工程师的原因之一，呃，因为我能把产品做出来，所以我赢了。

sentences.en: It, I would have never won if what I came in there was, was some kind of like crazy, uh, idea.
sentences.zh: 如果我走进去时提出的只是一些疯狂的、呃，想法，我是绝不可能获胜的。

sentences.en: I, I, I came in with a product.
sentences.zh: 我、我、我是带着产品走进来的。

sentences.en: I could demonstrate it.
sentences.zh: 我可以演示它。

sentences.en: And, and by.
sentences.zh: 而且，通过。

sentences.en: What I'm trying to say is that's, that's how everyone ends up winning.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，这就是每个人最终获胜的方式。

sentences.en: I, uh, at least in, in, in the meetings at Google, like I, I have, I certainly have never been able to just convince people.
sentences.zh: 我，呃，至少在谷歌的会议上，我、我，我肯定从来没有能够单靠说服别人来达到目的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Um, I, I've had an easier time with it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我，我的日子要好过一些。

sentences.en: Don't get me wrong.
sentences.zh: 别误会我的意思。

sentences.en: But like you, you, you always have to, uh, I think come in with the product.
sentences.zh: 但就像你，你，你总是必须，呃，我想带着产品来。

sentences.en: Usually, usually for me, the tide sort of, the tide tends to turn like when it's far too late.
sentences.zh: 通常，通常对我来说，风向、风向往往会在为时已晚的时候发生转变。

sentences.en: Like, like, like I, like I, I typically try to convince people of things, you know, early on, um,
sentences.zh: 就像，就像，就像我，像我，我通常试图在早期就说服人们相信某些事情，嗯，

sentences.en: and they only will get on board once it's become inevitable that that's what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 而他们只有在“我们正在这样做”已经成为不可避免的事实时，才会加入进来。

sentences.en: Like, and it's already sort of already happened.
sentences.zh: 就像，而且事情某种程度上已经发生了。

sentences.en: But, but I, but I do think that, um, like, yeah, I, I think what, what Chandler, what you're saying is right.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是，但我确实认为，嗯，就像，对，我觉得，钱德勒，你说的对。

sentences.en: It's like, yeah, that like often, oftentimes you're not going to convince people.
sentences.zh: 就像是，对，通常情况下，你往往无法说服别人。

sentences.en: You just have to go and find a way to show them.
sentences.zh: 你只能去寻找一种方法展示给他们看。

sentences.en: Um, I had one particular project recently where I sort of realized there's no way that I'm going to convince people if I don't just go show them on that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我最近有一个特定的项目，我当时意识到，如果我不直接去向他们展示，我是绝不可能说服他们的。

sentences.en: Although it turned out to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 尽管后来证明我的看法是错的。

sentences.en: I was able to convince them otherwise.
sentences.zh: 我还是成功说服了他们改变看法。

sentences.en: Um, but, but it's harder for, for, I still think that the, that the bar is different for, for, um.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，但是对……而言这更难，我仍然认为标准对于，呃……是不同的。

sentences.en: If you walk into a room and people don't expect you to be competent, then, then they will treat you differently.
sentences.zh: 如果你走进一个房间，而人们不期望你有能力，那么，他们就会以不同的方式对待你。

sentences.en: They will speak to you differently, but even worse, they will not listen to what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 他们会以不同的方式跟你说话，但更糟糕的是，他们不会听你在说什么。

sentences.en: And then, then the next person will speak and nobody will ever mention that I said anything.
sentences.zh: 然后，接下来另一个人发言，而没有人会提到我曾说过任何话。

sentences.en: And then, you know, four minutes later, a guy will say exactly what I had said four minutes earlier.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，四分钟后，一个男士会说出我四分钟前刚刚说过的话。

sentences.en: And then everybody will be like, oh yeah, very good point.
sentences.zh: 然后大家就会说，哦，对，说得太好了。

sentences.en: And I'm like, yo, yeah, no, but it's, I, I, yeah, I, I had, I had a manager go to me and said,
sentences.zh: 而我就想，嘿，不，但这是，我，我，我，我曾有一个经理对我说过，

sentences.en: Patricia, you need to be more, like, because I said that I would, people were stealing my work and, uh, you know.
sentences.zh: 帕特里夏，你需要更……因为我说过人们在窃取我的工作，呃，你知道的。

sentences.en: And he was like, ah, you have to be more assertive and you have to, like, like, like, say, I made that and blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，啊，你必须更自信一点，你必须，就像，就像，就像，说“这是我做的”云云。

sentences.en: And it's like, and, and so I was like, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 然后就像，于是我说，好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: Because, you know, that's how all of this process works.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，整个流程就是这样的。

sentences.en: It turns it against you.
sentences.zh: 它会把矛头指向你。

sentences.en: So it's you that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以错的是你。

sentences.en: It's not the system that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 错的不是系统。

sentences.en: It's you that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 错的是你。

sentences.en: And so I was like, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 所以我就想，好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: So the next time somebody presented my work as their work, I said, yeah, it's great that you could use the thing that I made to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以下次有人把我的工作说成是他们自己做的时候，我说，太棒了，你能用我做出来的东西来做这个。

sentences.en: And my boss was furious.
sentences.zh: 然后我的老板气炸了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was yelling at me.
sentences.zh: 对，他对我大喊大叫。

sentences.en: And I was like, I'm sorry, but this was what you told me to do.
sentences.zh: 我就说，对不起，但这就是你告诉我要做的。

sentences.en: It's like, I'm sorry, I can't win here.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，对不起，我在这里怎么都赢不了。

sentences.en: It's like, there's no, this is not a game that is winnable.
sentences.zh: 这就好像，没有，这不是一个能赢的游戏。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the only winning move is to, you know, go to a, go to a company or an organization where this does not happen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得唯一的赢法就是，你知道的，去一家不会发生这种事的公司或组织。

sentences.en: That's, that's, that's the winning move.
sentences.zh: 那，那，那才是赢法。

sentences.en: One thing I have, I have found tends to help here, at least in my experience is if there's something where I've said it, or I feel like,
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，我发现至少有一点通常很有帮助，那就是如果有些事情我已经说过，或者我觉得，

sentences.en: I feel like I'm answering the same question multiple times, or like I'm explaining something and like people just, people are just not hearing the words.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己像是在反复回答同一个问题，或者像是在解释某些事情，而人们就是，人们根本没听进去。

sentences.en: They're just hearing whatever they want in it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是听到了他们自己想听的。

sentences.en: That is often when I realize, okay, it is now time for me to write this down in some document or put it in slides or something.
sentences.zh: 通常在这个时候我就会意识到，好吧，现在是我把这些写进某个文档里，或者做成幻灯片什么的的时候了。

sentences.en: Um, and, and sort of, sort of to have some sort of paper trail where the next time that it comes up, I can just, instead of, instead of giving the explanation again,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，而且算是，算是留下一纸记录，这样下次再出现这种情况时，我就可以，与其，与其再次解释，

sentences.en: I can just point at, I'm not going to get into that right now.
sentences.zh: 我可以直接指出——我现在不想扯那个。

sentences.en: Look here, we've already done that.
sentences.zh: 看这里，我们已经做过了。

sentences.en: And here's the paper trail.
sentences.zh: 这就是书面记录。

sentences.en: And like, here's the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 看，这就是你问题的答案。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I had to do that all the time.
sentences.zh: 我不得不一直这样做。

sentences.en: There's no way for me to come into it.
sentences.zh: 我根本没有别的办法切入。

sentences.en: And, and that was also when my boss was like, yeah, why do you always bring a PowerPoint presentation to every meeting?
sentences.zh: 而且，那也是我老板说的时候，对啊，你为什么每次开会都要带个PPT演示文稿？

sentences.en: And I was like, not only do I bring a PowerPoint presentation to the meeting, I will send it in the invite.
sentences.zh: 而我说，我不但会在会上带PPT，我还会把它发在会议邀请里。

sentences.en: You, nobody can come and tell me that they did not see it or didn't get it.
sentences.zh: 你，没人能跑来跟我说他们没看见或者没收到。

sentences.en: And that it's not documented and timestamped.
sentences.zh: 而且这上面有据可查、有时间戳。

sentences.en: I've started in every meeting that I run, I take detailed minutes and I send them out.
sentences.zh: 我开始在我主持的每次会议上都做详细的会议纪要并发送出去。

sentences.en: And I, I almost never read the minutes, like immediately afterwards, a couple of the people who are on the meeting invites do read them and give feedback.
sentences.zh: 而且我，我几乎从不读会议纪要——就像会后马上，收到会议邀请的几个人确实会读并给出反馈。

sentences.en: So they are useful in that regard.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个角度来看，它们是有用的。

sentences.en: But the primary reason that I do this is that three or four or five times a year, I get asked for a paper trail on something.
sentences.zh: 但我这样做的主要原因是，一年下来总会有三四五次，有人找我要某件事的纸面记录。

sentences.en: And I now have this magical power where I can be like, that happened on this date, on this date, on this date.
sentences.zh: 而我现在有了一种神奇的能力，我可以这样说，那件事发生在这一天、这一天、还有这一天。

sentences.en: And we said, you said that, that, and that, and that.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，你说过这个、那个、那个，还有那个。

sentences.en: And it's just like, end of discussion.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，讨论到此结束。

sentences.en: I had a wonderful, like he, two, two mentors or bosses, I guess, at some point in my career.
sentences.zh: 我曾有过一段非常美好的经历，在我职业生涯的某个阶段，他，有两个导师或老板吧。

sentences.en: And they had a very good, like motto.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个很好的座右铭。

sentences.en: They said that the people who write the minutes decide what was said.
sentences.zh: 他们说，写会议纪要的人决定了说了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, so they said, whenever you are in like a meeting, especially if it's antagonistic in some way, you make sure you are the ones writing the minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以他们说，每当你开会时，尤其是带有某种对抗性质的会议，你一定要确保自己是写纪要的那个人。

sentences.en: And this is, if you look at the history of the COBOL programming language, which was the first language developed by a committee.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看COBOL编程语言的历史，它是第一门由委员会开发的语言。

sentences.en: That's one of the, and it's, COBOL is a very interesting language because it was developed in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 这是其中之一，而且，COBOL是一门非常有趣的语言，因为它是在20世纪60年代开发的。

sentences.en: And most of the primary people behind its development were women.
sentences.zh: 其开发背后的主力军大部分是女性。

sentences.en: Well, how did that come to be?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是怎么回事呢？

sentences.en: Well, two reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有两个原因。

sentences.en: One, at that time, being an engineer or a programmer was not, you know, the cool thing.
sentences.zh: 第一，在那个时候，当工程师或程序员可不是什么，你知道的，很酷的事。

sentences.en: It was, it was, it was all about being a businessman, the business logic.
sentences.zh: 当时，当时，一切都关乎商人，关乎商业逻辑。

sentences.en: So most of the technical people involved were women.
sentences.zh: 所以参与其中的大部分技术人员都是女性。

sentences.en: But two, who took the minutes in those meetings?
sentences.zh: 但第二，是谁在那些会议上做记录的？

sentences.en: Who was the one that was running the meetings where they were developing COBOL?
sentences.zh: 谁是开发COBOL的那些会议的主持人？

sentences.en: It was always the women that the heads of all of the subgroups of the COBOL committee, like, I think like 60 or 70% of them were women.
sentences.zh: 一直都是女性，COBOL委员会各个小组的负责人中，嗯，我想大概有60%或70%都是女性。

sentences.en: And like, there is an incredible power in being the person that is running the meeting or that takes the minutes.
sentences.zh: 而且，成为开会的人或做会议纪要的人拥有令人难以置信的力量。

sentences.en: Like you get to literally write history.
sentences.zh: 就像你可以字面意义上地书写历史一样。

sentences.en: So, I'm just curious, should we try and get back to your questions or do you want to just keep going?
sentences.zh: 所以，我很好奇，我们是要回到你的问题上，还是你想继续讲下去？

sentences.zh: 那么，那么，那么，那么，克鲁斯先生。
